"Let your light shine" Matthew 5:16
Welcome to High Ash Church of England School
Message from our Headteacher
Welcome to High Ash School’s website. We hope you find it helpful and informative.
I am proud to be Headteacher and to work with our children, staff, parents, church and community so that together we can “let our light shine.” Every child has the right to “Grow Together and Shine Forever” as High Ash Stars, guided by our PROUD principles and Christian values.
We aim for high academic achievement while also developing caring, responsible individuals who make a positive difference in society. Our motto, “Let your light shine” (Matthew 5:16), chosen by the children, reflects this vision.
Our dedicated staff provide a rich curriculum, opportunities for reflection and worship, and constant encouragement so every child can thrive academically, morally, and spiritually.
If you share this vision, we warmly invite you to visit and see our school in action. More details can be found on our ‘About Us’ and ‘School Information’ pages.
I look forward to working with you to help every child shine.

pageCache.text:
"Let your light shine" Matthew 5:16
Our Curriculum
french
Bienvenue! At High Ash, children begin learning French in Key Stage 2 (Years 3–6) through the engaging Kapow scheme of work. Lessons are fun and interactive, using songs, rhymes, role play and games to bring the language to life.
Our French curriculum aims to instil a love of language learning and an appreciation of other cultures. We want pupils to develop the confidence to communicate in French for practical purposes, using both spoken and written language. The scheme is carefully designed to provide a strong foundation for future language learning, while also deepening understanding of English grammar and opening up opportunities for study and work in other countries later in life.
Learning is structured around three key knowledge strands — phonics, vocabulary and grammar — which are applied through the skills of listening, speaking, reading and writing. In Year 3/4, the focus is mainly on oral skills, with written French gradually introduced throughout the year. Pronunciation is taught explicitly. All lessons are adapted to meet the needs of all learners.
By the end of Key Stage 2, pupils will be able to:
- Engage in purposeful dialogue in real-life situations (e.g. ordering food, asking for directions).
- Speak, read and write simple texts with confidence and accurate pronunciation.
- Use strategies such as recognising cognates and applying grammar rules to understand and construct language.
- Demonstrate understanding of spoken French through active listening and appropriate responses.
- Apply their skills to other languages in the future.
- Through this approach, we ensure pupils meet the National Curriculum expectations for Languages and leave High Ash as confident, curious learners with a lifelong love of languages.

pageCache.pageTitle: High Ash C of E Primary - Reading & Phonics
pageCache.text:
"Let your light shine" Matthew 5:16
Our Curriculum
Reading & Phonics
Reading & Phonics
At High Ash, reading is at the heart of our curriculum. We believe every child deserves to be a confident, fluent and curious reader.
Phonics Lead and Interim Reading Lead – Mrs Natalie Barrasford
Reading Lead – Mrs Ella Derham (Maternity Leave 2026-27)
Early Reading in Key Stage One
In Years One and Two, the children follow the RWI Phonics Scheme and progress through stages which build on their blending, developing fluency, accuracy and understanding.
Guided by the evidence-informed pedagogy of Christopher Such (The Art and Science of Teaching Primary Reading), we aim to balance the rigorous mechanics of decoding with explicit comprehension teaching, rich vocabulary development and a genuine love of reading.
The children's reading journey begins with a focus on decoding and fluency.
Phonics First: We use the Read Write Inc. (RWI) programme to deliver systematic, synthetic phonics instruction, giving early readers the foundational tools they need to decode with confidence. Children who require support to keep up have 1:1 daily phonics tutoring.
Matched Practice: Children take home decodable reading books closely aligned with their current phonics stage, ensuring success and building early independence.
Shared Storytelling: Alongside their decodable book, every child chooses a library book to take home for an adult to read to them.
Once children are assessed as 'readers' and can decode fluently, they move to guided reading sessions designed to develop Accuracy, Automaticity, Prosody and Comprehension.
Whole-Class High-Quality Texts: Our daily reading lessons bring the entire class together to read rich, diverse and challenging texts.
Curriculum Triangulation: Where possible, our main reading texts complement our foundation curriculum topics. This deliberate alignment deepens children’s background knowledge, reinforces subject-specific vocabulary and turns reading into a powerful tool for discovering the world.
Fluency at the Core: Through echo reading, choral reading, and targeted teacher modelling, children learn to read not just accurately, but with expressiveness and rhythm (prosody), unlocking deeper comprehension and critical inference.
Assessment & Support: To ensure no child falls behind, we track progress using regular assessments alongside national benchmarks at Key Stage 1 and 2. We deliver targeted, phonics interventions to ensure children have the support they need to succeed in becoming confident readers.
Reading for Pleasure
Teaching children how to read is only half our mission; inspiring them to choose to read is the other.
A Thriving School Library: Every class enjoys dedicated weekly library time to browse, discuss, and choose from our selection of fiction, non-fiction, and poetry.
Year 6 Reading Ambassadors: Our pupil leaders maintain our library space, champion new arrivals, recommend titles to younger peers and run lunchtime reading groups.
Author Visits & Book Clubs: We regularly host published authors.
Community Partnerships: Through close ties with local independent bookshops, we keep our library shelves freshly stocked with diverse, contemporary texts and offer discounted books directly to our families.
"When we teach a child to read, we give them a skill; when we inspire a child to read, we give them the world."

pageCache.text:
"Let your light shine" Matthew 5:16
Our Curriculum
Science
At High Ash, we spark curiosity, inspire critical thinking, and empower every child to view themselves as a scientist. Our Science curriculum equips pupils with the tools, vocabulary, and investigative skills needed to understand, question, and shape the world around them.
Our Vision & Core Objectives
Inspire World-Ready Scientists: We provide opportunities for all children to develop the skills and passion required to become scientists and work scientifically within the wider world
Nurture Curiosity & Connections: We encourage all children to build an interest and curiosity in Science, finding links between historical and modern scientific discoveries.
Develop Independent Thinkers: We equip children to critically engage with Science—enabling them to think independently, question, investigate, and discover.
Master Scientific Language: We provide pupils with the essential scientific tools and vocabulary needed to explain and understand the practical uses of Science.
National Curriculum Alignment
Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS): Science learning begins in Reception through the EYFS Statutory Framework under the Understanding the World area of learning, where pupils explore the natural world and observe changes over time.
Key Stage 1 (Years 1 & 2): Following the Key Stage 1 Science Programme of Study, children focus on firsthand practical experiences, exploring everyday materials, plants, animals, and seasonal changes.
Lower Key Stage 2 (Years 3 & 4): In line with the Lower Key Stage 2 Science Programme of Study, pupils broaden their scientific view through testing materials, forces, rocks, habitats, and light.
Upper Key Stage 2 (Years 5 & 6): Adhering to the Upper Key Stage 2 Science Programme of Study, pupils encounter complex concepts including evolution, electricity, Earth and space, and light, while conducting systematic fair tests.
Working Scientifically: Across all key stages, practical scientific enquiry skills are embedded into topic teaching, following statutory Working Scientifically Objectives.
How Science is Taught & Structured
To ensure high-quality, consistent science delivery across all year groups, learning follows a structured teaching sequence supported by high-quality schemes including Plymouth Science planning and PLAN Primary Science Assessment resources:
Retrieval & Recap: Every lesson begins by reviewing previous key vocabulary, concepts, and scientific enquiry types. Teachers recap prior learning from recent lessons, as well as previous terms or years, to embed long-term memory.
Explicit Modeling: Teachers introduce new knowledge clearly using visual aids, physical resources, and precise scientific language.
Targeted Questioning: Continuous checking for understanding allows teachers to probe deeper, address misconceptions, and stretch thinking.
Independent & Practical Practice: Pupils apply their knowledge through varied activities and different types of scientific enquiry.
Classroom Environment & Working Walls
Every classroom maintains an interactive learning environment designed to scaffold enquiry:
Enquiry Types & Skills Displays: Prompts and posters clearly identify the active enquiry type (e.g., fair testing, classifying, pattern seeking) so children understand how they are working scientifically.
Key Vocabulary & Diagrams: Displays showcase essential technical terms, scientific diagrams, visual symbols, and photographs to support learning.
Inclusive Provision & SEND Support
We ensure Science is accessible to all learners, enabling every child to achieve optimal progress:
Vocabulary Access: Key terms and visual glossaries are readily available in all classrooms.
Adapted Tasks: Instructions, tasks, and resources are modified where necessary without reducing learning ambition.
Targeted Adult Support: Adult guidance is strategically deployed during practical investigations and written tasks.
Assessment & Progression
Pupil progress is tracked through ongoing formative assessment and end-of-unit evaluations:
Continuous Checking: Start-of-lesson quizzes, vocabulary checks, and fill-in-the-blank activities gauge retention and readiness.
Teacher Assessment: Work is evaluated against clear Learning Intentions (LIs) using green/yellow marking criteria.
Unit Reviews: Comprehensive end-of-unit assessments using PLAN assessment tools evaluate both substantive knowledge and working scientifically skills.
Book Expectations: Pupil books feature a Knowledge Organiser at the start of each unit, clear dates and LIs, and evidence of varied enquiry types and adapted work.

We focus on building strong understanding, using clear mathematical language, and encouraging every child to think like a mathematician. pageCache.text:
"Let your light shine" Matthew 5:16
Our Curriculum
music
music
Music at High Ash – A Joyful Part of School Life
At High Ash, music is so much more than a subject on the timetable – it’s a chance for our children to shine, express themselves, and discover the joy of performing. Our engaging and diverse curriculum ensures every child gets the chance to experience music in a way that is fun, memorable, and fully in line with the National Curriculum.
Whether it’s learning to play instruments together in class, singing their hearts out in assemblies, or taking part in school performances, our pupils are building confidence as well as musical skills. We love seeing how music brings children together, encouraging teamwork, creativity, and a real sense of pride.
As one of our pupils put it, “I love when we all play together because it feels like being in a real band!” Moments like these show how much joy music brings to our school community.
We also explore music from different times and places, helping children see just how powerful and universal it is. By the time they leave High Ash, pupils take with them not only knowledge and skills, but a lifelong love of music that will stay with them long after their primary years.

Our Curriculum
Art and Design
Art and Design
At High Ash School, art is a valued part of the curriculum, encouraging children to explore their creativity, imagination, and self-expression. Pupils are introduced to a wide range of artistic techniques, materials, and styles, helping them develop key skills in drawing, painting, sculpture, and mixed media.
There is clear evidence of progression in art, supported by success criteria that help children reflect on and improve their work. Teachers provide 1:1 modelling when needed, and additional support is given to ensure every child can take part and achieve success.
Through studying the work of artists from different cultures and periods, children gain inspiration and learn to appreciate the role of art in society. Lessons are designed to nurture confidence, individuality, and resilience, while providing opportunities for pupils to experiment and take creative risks.

Our Curriculum
Computing
Computing
Computing skills are a cornerstone in fostering ambition, confidence, creativity, and independence in our learners. At High Ash, we strive to give children every opportunity to succeed in computing. As pupils progress through our school, they will develop robust computing knowledge and skills — understanding algorithms, computational thinking, and data — alongside a stronger understanding of online safety and how to protect themselves in digital environments.
“Everybody in this country should learn to program a computer, because it teaches you how to think.” — Steve Jobs
We share that belief at High Ash: computing is not just a technical skill but a way of thinking, and we encourage our children to engage with and value the computing curriculum, always asking why they are learning — not just how. We want them to reflect on, discuss, and appreciate how computing enhances their learning, development, and wellbeing. Achieving a healthy balance with technology is key to effective education and a fulfilling lifestyle.
Our curriculum is built around the National Centre for Computing Education’s Teach Computing Curriculum, ensuring our provision is grounded in the latest DfE-endorsed research and practice.
By the end of Year Six, children will understand:
At High Ash, we empower our children not just to navigate the digital world, but to excel within it. Building upon foundations drawn from subjects like Maths, Science, and Design Technology, learners are encouraged to explore computing systems and understand how they interact. Given the rapid evolution of technology — including the growing role of artificial intelligence and data — our curriculum ensures pupils become digitally literate learners who are equipped to adapt, overcome challenges, make informed choices, and integrate new learning, all in preparation for a future shaped by constant innovation. We are also mindful of the national curriculum changes on the horizon — including a greater focus on AI and data literacy — and are starting to prepare our provision now so that High Ash pupils are ready for the more digitally-focused curriculum planned for 2028.

We will continue to adapt and enhance our curriculum to ensure it meets the needs of all learners, including those with disabilities, ensuring every child at High Ash thrives in a digitally rich and inclusive learning environment.

Geography
Geography
At High Ash, we aim to provide children with a rich and engaging geography curriculum that develops both their knowledge and skills, helping them make sense of the world around them. We encourage critical thinking by enabling pupils to ask perceptive questions, analyse evidence and explain their ideas clearly. Fieldwork is a key part of our approach, with opportunities for hands-on learning built into each year group. We also nurture a strong interest in our pupils’ own locality, while helping them to understand how it compares and contrasts with other parts of the world. Throughout their journey, children gain growing confidence in using geographical concepts, terms and vocabulary with accuracy.

Our Curriculum
PE
At High Ash, we believe physical activity is essential for children’s healthy development, emotional wellbeing, and academic success. PE and sport help pupils grow stronger, manage stress, focus better, and build positive relationships. Through lessons, children develop physical skills and fitness, learn to compete fairly and co-operate with others, value creativity and skilled performance and understand both teamwork and individual responsibility.
We deliver a high-quality, broad and balanced PE curriculum that meets National Curriculum requirements and inspires all pupils to succeed and excel in a wide range of physical activities. Our approach, using the PE Planning scheme, ensures:
Every child has the opportunity to become physically confident, supporting their health and fitness in and out of school.
All pupils can swim at least 25m and understand basic water safety before leaving primary school.
High-energy lessons build fitness and resilience.
Activities are adapted so all children, including those with additional needs, can participate fully.
Opportunities to compete in sport and physical activities develop character and promote values such as fairness, respect, leadership, cooperation, and tolerance.
Children receive two PE lessons each week – one taught by a specialist PE coach and one by their class teacher. Both follow carefully planned units from PE Planning, with resources prepared in advance to maximise learning time. Beyond lessons, pupils take part in sports days, clubs, and inter-school competitions, helping them to build skills, confidence, and a lifelong enjoyment of physical activity.

pageCache.text:
"Let your light shine" Matthew 5:16
Our Curriculum
history
History at High Ash
At High Ash, we aim to inspire a lifelong curiosity about the past, empowering children to understand their place in the world and appreciate how history shapes our present. Through an engaging, carefully sequenced curriculum aligned with the National Curriculum and enriched by Kapow History resources, our learners leave each topic with a deep sense of identity, community, and global awareness.
Our approach combines strong substantive knowledge with rigorous historical enquiry skills, ensuring children do not just learn about history—they learn how to think like historians.
Our Approach
Chronological Frameworks & Context: Children build a secure, interconnected mental timeline from ancient civilisations and local history through to modern times, developing a clear grasp of how key periods, empires, and events fit together.
Disciplinary Enquiry & Source Analysis: Through unit enquiry questions, children actively interrogate primary and secondary sources, evaluate artefacts, analyse historical interpretations, and explore cause, consequence, and continuity over time.
Enriched & Cross-Curricular Learning: History lessons are enriched with meaningful links to geography, art, literacy, and computing, helping children make connections across subjects while supporting long-term knowledge retention.
Inclusive Scaffolding & High Challenge: Lessons are designed to be accessible to all learners. Scaffolded tasks, visual models, sentence stems, and accessible vocabulary banks ensure every child—including those with SEND—can access high-level learning and make optimal progress.
Clear Progression & Consistency: Our structured spiral framework ensures clear progression across year groups, constantly recapping and building upon prior knowledge, key concepts, and historical vocabulary to give teachers the clarity to deliver consistently high-quality history teaching.

pageCache.text:
"Let your light shine" Matthew 5:16
WRAParound care
WRAParound care
We offer before and after-school care through our wraparound provision and recognise this is an essential service for many parents. We manage this service ourselves to ensure the quality of provision. Our wraparound service is based in our Ash Tree dining room but uses the outdoor space as much as possible if the weather allows. There are a range of activities on offer, from sports, arts and crafts, board games and toys, IT, and plenty of scope to just read and relax.
Numbers are limited based on the space and staff available and places must be booked in advance via MyChildAtSchool.
Breakfast sessions are available from 7.45am with breakfast and 8.15am excluding breakfast. We offer two options after-school too, pick up by either 5pm or 6pm. Children can choose from toast or cereal if they would like breakfast, and we have a rotating menu of hot and cold snacks for tea (usually served around 4.30pm).

Our Curriculum
Design & Technology
Design & Technology
Our Vision and Inclusive Approach
At High Ash School, Design and Technology is a dynamic, practical subject that prepares every child for the future by inspiring them to become creative, curious, and resilient problem solvers. We foster an inclusive learning environment where all pupils, regardless of starting point or individual needs, are supported to access every aspect of the curriculum. Through adapted tools, tailored scaffolding, and flexible tasks, we ensure every child develops essential life skills, resourcefulness, and creative confidence.
High Ash designers begin their journey in the Foundation Stage and progressively expand their knowledge throughout their primary years. Utilising the National Curriculum alongside Kapow Primary, our learning sequence covers six core technical areas: Cooking & Nutrition, Textiles, Structures, Electrical Systems, Mechanical Systems, and Digital World. By connecting with subjects like science, mathematics, art, and computing, children learn to apply their knowledge in real-world contexts while developing the technical vocabulary needed to communicate their ideas clearly.

Listening to Readers in School
Reading is an essential life-skill, reaching far beyond a child's time in school. We want our children to develop a love of reading that will help them flourish as they progress through our school and make their way in the world. "Let your light shine" Matthew 5:16
Our Children as Leaders
Our Children as Leaders
At High Ash, we greatly value the input of our pupils in to how our school is run so that they get to live out the vision of our school and also understand the value of service and contribution.
So, what leaders do we have?
1. Reflection Leaders- pupils in KS2 work with me to plan and deliver our Reflections.
2. Junior Leadership Team (School Council)- this elected group work to ensure we improve our school. They have had impact on our behaviour policy, on lunchtimes, play equipment and on the library area.
3. Eco Squad- this social action group has campaigned over the last four years to reduce plastic and waste in our school. Our school is now 96% plastic free and we are getting close to being 100% plastic free by 2024. They award classes for recycling and also volunteer to litter pick at breaktimes.
4. Y6 Ambassadors- each week, 3 different children from Y6 plan and deliver our Star Reflection on a Friday.
5. Librarians- a dedicated team of librarians give up their time to keep the library tidy and also recommend books to others.
6. Play Leaders - a team of Year 6 children lead and support games with the younger children during lunchtimes
We are so proud of how our children are living out our vision and letting their light shine!

pageCache.pageTitle: High Ash C of E Primary - Writing
pageCache.text:
"Let your light shine" Matthew 5:16
Our Curriculum
Writing
At High Ash School, every child is nurtured to become an empowered, confident and independent writer who can consistently write in grammatically correct sentences across the curriculum. English teaching is engaging, motivating and personalised, with writing taught through a structured, skills-based approach. Each unit follows a clear sequence: children read and evaluate diverse, ambitious and varied writing prompts, discuss a WAGOLL (‘What a good one looks like’), practise key skills through extensive teacher modelling with opportunities to embed their learning at every stage. The work culminates in a final Star Write which showcases their learning and provides recognition and a chance to celebrate 'Clever Writers' with a weekly certificate.
Learning is supported through the I Am A Clever Writer approach, ensuring progression across the school and the use of checklists to layer and embed writing skills. Phonics strategies such as 'hold a sentence' support the children's ability to orally rehearse sentences before they write. Teachers build ‘working walls’ across the week with modelled examples, vocabulary, and checklists which pupils use in every lesson. We recognise that great writers are built on firm foundations. We are rigorous with the 'basics' so children are confident to then layer higher level skills into their writing. Scaffolds and adaptations are included in every lesson to ensure all children are able to access and achieve the learning intention.
Children are encouraged to use ambitious vocabulary in both their oral and written work, they are given purposeful opportunities to write in a range of forms for different audiences, often linked to class topics and interests.
At High Ash we have high expectations for handwriting and presentation. We believe that developing a mature, speedy joined handwriting style increases children’s motivation and their belief in themselves as writers. Writing involves many processes, so having fluent handwriting is one less thing to think about.
A holistic and consistent approach is applied to handwriting lessons, supported by the Letter Village Handwriting scheme provided by our Read, Write Inc provider.
Explicit handwriting lessons are taught regularly throughout the school year with targeted support available for children identified as needing additional repeated practice.

pageCache.text:

ABout us
I am very proud to be the Headteacher of High Ash School and enjoy working with the children, staff, parents, Church and wider community to ensure we can be the very best we can and all 'let our light shine'.
We believe that every child has the right to ‘Grow Together and Shine Forever’ as High Ash Stars through following our PROUD principles and our school vision of letting our light shine as Good Samaritans. The children chose our school motto as they felt it represented our ethos and spirit as a church school.
Our rich, broad and balanced curriculum is ambitious for all children and enables all pupils to make excellent progress. We also consider the whole child and aim to develop individuals who will make a positive contribution to society and are able to truly live our PROUD principles and have a moral compass underpinned by Christian values. We wish them to know and understand how to be a light and inspiration to themselves and others and this was the reason the children chose ‘Let your light shine’ (Matthew 5:16) in order to represent this.
Our website includes a lot of information that I hope you will find useful. However, if you wish for your child to join High Ash, we warmly welcome you to arrange a visit.
I look forward to meeting you soon.

School Information
REmote learning
REmote learning
Occasionally, there may be unforeseen circumstances such as severe weather conditions, power failures, or lack of water, which mean the school may need to close to ensure the safety of our pupils and staff. Where possible, announcements will be made before the start of the school day, but this is not always possible.
How to Find Out If School is Closed
We will communicate about any school closures through the following official channels:
Remote Learning Procedures - short term
There is no expectation for teachers to deliver live lessons during short-term severe weather closures of one or two days. Work will be set for the day and will include activities related to the current topic as well as maths and English tasks appropriate to the age group. The work will be sent home via Google Classroom for the older year groups or via email to parents for younger years.
Remote Learning Procedures - long term
Where a closure is anticipated to be longer than two days, or where the closure is planned, the remote education plan below will be followed.
